newsitem.title: CROATIA: Pliva 1996 net HRK 456 mln, up 14.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Pliva 1996 net HRK 456 mln, up 14.4 pct.

text.p: Croatia's leading drugs firm Pliva said on Friday it posted a net profit of 456 million kuna ($84 million) in 1996, an increase of 14.39 percent from a year earlier.
Pre-tax profit rose 30.9 percent to 616 million kuna ($113 million), it said in a news release. Pliva attributed the increase to "stronger sales, royalties income and considerable cost reduction".
"The growth rate for net profit was lower than for pre-tax (profit) because of a higher tax base than in 1995," company president Zeljko Covic told reporters.
Pliva's total 1996 income rose 9.42 percent to 2.274 billion kuna ($418 million). Of this, 2.045 billion kuna was accounted for by sales alone, Covic said.
Pliva is proposing a per share dividend of 248 kuna for 1996. It paid shareholders 235 kuna per ordinary share on 1995 results.
Total 1996 dividend payout will rise to 135 million kuna from 114.5 million, Covic said.
Pliva's ordinary shares were split 37-for-1 and reissued with a face value of 100 kuna each in January this year.
Its 1/5 GDRs, listed on the London Stock Exchange, rose to $16.2 each on Friday morning from $15.9 at Thursday's close. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
